3.0.s.en: (1) The sending of Timothy to them

3.0.0.en: Paul had an intense longing to be reassured about the Thessalonians, and since he was unable to come to them himself because of the Jews' opposition, he preferred that he and Silas alone remain in Athens, and he sent the disciple dearest to his heart, Timothy, to Thessalonica, and in humility calls him "our brother, and minister of God, and our fellowlabourer," to complete their evangelization and exhortation so that they might stand firm in the faith.

3.1.0.en: Appointed thereunto: the Apostles, together with the rest of the believers, are exposed to persecutions that test them and prove them.

3.1.1.en: The Apostle feared that some of them might lack depth of faith and forsake Christ because of the Jews' persecution of them, for he had already told them that affliction and persecution are not strange in the life of the Christian, because they are a test of his faith.

3.2.0.en: St. Paul reminds them that when he was with them before this time, he told them that storms of persecution must break upon them and upon him also in the city of Thessalonica, and this indeed happened, and all the believers there knew of it, and because of it he was compelled to leave Thessalonica and go to Berea (Acts 17:5-10).

3.2.1.en: Let us be strong when sufferings meet us, and let us not doubt the love of God the Father because of sorrows and hard circumstances, for He permits them for our edification: they give us spiritual firmness, free us from all negligence, make us feel for our afflicted brethren, and urge us to cling to Him and lean on Him, so that we grow deeper spiritually.

3.3.0.en: When I could no longer forbear: I could not bear patiently the lack of news from you and my fear for you, that you might be shaken by the Jews' persecution of you.

3.3.1.en: Because I knew with certainty that temptation must come upon you, I sent to you to learn whether our preaching was still alive in you, and to be sure that you were still standing firm in the faith and that the fruit of our labor had not been lost.

3.4.0.en: When Timothy returned from Thessalonica, he brought Paul good tidings of the steadfastness of their faith, the abundance of their love, their constant remembrance of him and their longing to see him, just as Paul too had a great longing to see them and always remembered them in his thought. So we notice the prayers and the feelings of mutual love between the two sides.

3.5.0.en: Our necessity: necessary needs that he does not obtain, that is, he suffers in obtaining the barest necessities such as food or rest.

3.5.1.en: Your faith and your sincerity overflowed in us with comfort and joy in spite of all the difficulties we pass through. The Apostle was surrounded by outward circumstances of sorrow, but in his heart there was joy because he was reassured about the believers.

3.6.0.en: Paul had feared that the faith of the Thessalonians would be shaken, but when Timothy came and told him of the steadfastness of their faith, this news refreshed Paul's heart as if life had returned to him, that is, he enjoyed rest and joy.

3.7.0.en: The Apostle feels that any thanks he offers to God is little and not proportionate to His grace and to the joy with which He compensated him when he heard of the steadfastness of the faith of the Thessalonians. Here Paul's joy at the success of his ministry is seen to be greater than his concern for his personal comfort, for the true servant rejoices in the success of his ministry more than in anything, and the sign of that is the steadfastness of those he serves in the Lord and not their attachment to his own person.

3.7.1.en: Give thanks to God for all His gifts, and for the faith and rest of those around you, and for every work He brings to success through your hands, because thanksgiving gladdens your heart and strengthens you and others in the faith.

3.8.s.en: (3) His wishes to see them and for their growth

3.8.0.en: St. Paul was not seeking bodily rest, but worked and struggled night and day in prayers for the Thessalonians. Preaching, for him, was not merely sermons and holding meetings; rather, he always carried in his mind those who had believed and hoped to return to them to complete their evangelization, that is, what was lacking of his teaching to them, in order to establish their faith.

3.9.0.en: God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ: here is a clear witness to the unity of the Father and the Son.

3.9.1.en: The Apostle did not say that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ direct (in the dual) our way, because the Father and the Son are one in the divine essence.

3.9.2.en: Direct our way unto you: make our arrival at Thessalonica easy, and guide us and support us in completing your evangelization and ministry.

3.9.3.en: Paul asks that God help him to reach Thessalonica and complete his ministry there.

3.10.0.en: The Apostle says: whether I come to you or am unable to come, God is able to increase your love for one another in the Church of Thessalonica and toward all men, even as we also love you with great love.

3.11.0.en: Establishing in holiness is a continuing process, that is, we grow in holiness until Christ comes in His Second Coming, full of glory with all His saints, and we stand before the judgment seat of Christ where we are found blameless, a glorious Church, holy and without blemish.

3.11.1.en: May you be ambitious for spiritual growth, so that you long for your prayers and your knowledge of the Holy Bible to increase, and your love and your service to others to increase also, so that you experience each day what is new in the love of God. Holiness, love and the resurrection

4.0.s.en: (1) Holiness and the rejection of fornication

4.0.0.en: St. Paul calls the believers in Thessalonica to hold fast to the Christian conduct that pleases God, and even to grow in it.

4.1.0.en: St. Paul reminds them of the earlier teachings they received from him, which guide them to the way of holiness. It is beautiful of the Apostle to put "the Lord Jesus" in everything: in (v. 1) he says "we beseech you ... by the Lord Jesus," and here he says "what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus." For when Christ is the goal, all our actions are in the right direction, not merely carrying out commandments but being careful to please God and working to increase, that is, spiritual growth, until we reach holiness.

4.2.0.en: God has set us apart from the world and sanctified us and dedicated us to Himself. For the sake of this holiness he calls them to reject fornication, which was bound up with the idolatrous worship out of which these Thessalonians had come, for the lust of the flesh was part of their former religion.

4.3.1.en: The Apostle speaks here of purity in the relationship between husband and wife, as he said in (Heb 13:4), so that a person does not apply the lusts and perversions of the world within his marital relationship, but feels the presence of Christ with him in this relationship, so that it is an expression of love, and he considers the feelings of the other and keeps away from any perversion practiced by the people of the world.

4.4.0.en: Not knowing God is the fountain of impurity. Because the pagan Gentiles do not know the happiness of life with God, sexual passions are their paradise, and they understand nothing of marriage but passion and lust with all their perversions, to fill the emptiness of their hearts.

4.5.0.en: The Apostle affirms the teaching he had already given, which is that no one should go beyond and covet the wives of others or any unmarried woman, a matter that is a grave violation of the commandment of the Lord Christ in (Mt 5:27, 28), for God avenges those who regard fornication as permissible.

4.6.0.en: In view of the holy calling with which we were called, we must live in holiness and keep away from these things, not only because we fear God's vengeance and discipline, but because our life is purity and holiness.

4.7.0.en: He who despises the commandment does not dishonor only his own body and the body of another, but dishonors God, who gave us His Holy Spirit to give us strength and help to be holy and blameless before Him. Therefore whoever defiles his body dishonors the Holy Spirit, who sanctified his body by the sacrament of the Holy Myron.

4.7.1.en: Put Christ before you in all your steps and in your relationship with the opposite sex, and do not allow your eyes or your mind to be defiled by the evil of the world. And when you draw near to your wife, remember Christ who blesses you, so that you behave with propriety and love and consider her feelings.

4.8.0.en: The Thessalonians needed to be written to about holiness, because they were liable to fall back into their old habits, while brotherly love was the distinguishing mark of the life of that Church and the secret of its success.

4.8.1.en: How we wish that the spirit of love would prevail in our churches today, for the weakness of the Church in any age is the result of its lack of love. Love is the fruit of the new nature given to all who are born of God and who are in constant and continual fellowship with Him, and it is very important and essential in our Christian life.

4.9.1.en: Macedonia: the northern part of Greece, whose capital was Thessalonica.

4.9.2.en: The believers of Thessalonica practiced brotherly love toward all the believers in Macedonia, and the Apostle was glad of that when Timothy brought him the good news of their faith and love, but he asks them to increase more and more, for growth and increase are necessary in the Christian life, since we learn them from the commandments of Christ and His redemption of us, and they are accomplished by continual striving.

4.10.1.en: He also enjoins them to be quiet in dealing with others so that they may live in peace, and that each one should carry out his responsibilities and his work, so that he is not a burden to others.

4.11.0.en: Them that are without: that is, the unbelievers.

4.11.1.en: Unbelievers keep their eyes open to watch the conduct of the believers, the members of the new religion, and likewise the rulers of the nation watch them. So walk in the way that makes them see in you a community that goes about its work in quietness and peace, and faithful citizens who fear God and work diligently to the extent that meets their needs, so that you do not stretch out your hands to anyone.

4.11.2.en: Take care to fulfill your responsibilities and do not wait until others demand them of you, but try to help others instead of demanding their help, and in this way you show your love for them in practice and become an image of Christ, who gave Himself for the world.

4.12.s.en: (3) The resurrection and the Second Coming

4.12.0.en: The Apostle does not rebuke the believers for their grief at the loss of their loved ones, but comforts them, saying of them that they are "asleep," that is, sleeping, in the hope of the resurrection, so they should not grieve like the rest who believe in the annihilation of man by death.

4.13.0.en: If we believe that the Lord Jesus died and raised Himself, then the believers who have fallen asleep, and about whose fate you feel anxious, the Lord will raise up and bring with Him alive, for He is the Head and we are the members of the body, and what happens to the Head must happen to the members also.

4.14.0.en: St. Paul declares the sequence of the events that will take place at the Second Coming of Christ: those who will be alive at this coming will not precede the dead, meaning that they will not be ahead in entering the Kingdom of Heaven before those who have fallen asleep.

4.15.0.en: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven and command the dead to rise from the sleep of death and come forth to eternal life. The three expressions, a shout, the voice of the archangel, the trump of God, are meant to declare the greatness of Christ's Second Coming. What is meant by the resurrection from the dead here is the resurrection of the bodies, for the spirits of the dead continue to live since they departed from the body, that is, the spirit does not die, so the bodies raised from the dead are united with the spirits to stand before God the Judge, and this happens first, that is, the living do not enter the Kingdom before those who have fallen asleep, but those who have fallen asleep rise and all enter together at one time.

4.16.0.en: Caught up: the believers in Christ will be caught up, that is, lifted up to heaven to meet Christ, and He will bring them into His Kingdom. The rapture takes place on the day of judgment, at the moment of entering the Kingdom, and not before this, as some sects believe.

4.16.1.en: As for those who will be alive at the Second Coming, they will be taken quickly, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, to meet Christ in the heavenly glories, after their bodies are changed into the likeness of the body of Christ after His resurrection. All the laws of gravity will be cast aside, because the very power of God which raised the Lord Jesus from the dead and seated Him in glory is what will carry His saints into the air and the clouds.

4.16.2.en: Our meeting Him before He reaches the earth is a proof of our intense longing for Him and our not fearing the judgment, the fear that drives the wicked to hide from Him.

4.17.0.en: The Apostle asks them to repeat these words in one another's hearing and to be comforted concerning the temporary separation from loved ones.

4.17.1.en: Eternity is not far from you, and Christ wants to lift you up with Him to the Kingdom. May you cast your sins from you and draw near to God in prayers, and not be troubled by afflictions because they are temporary, for your Christ will compensate you for all this with joys that cannot be expressed.

4.17.2.en: Christian conduct and preparation for the Second Coming

5.0.s.en: (1) Preparation for the coming of Christ

5.0.0.en: Some believers err in trying, by calculations, to predict the time of the Second Coming. The Apostle told them when he was with them that no one knows the time of Christ's coming, so he sees no need to repeat what he had already explained to them.

5.1.1.en: St. Paul repeats his statement that the time of the Lord's coming is unknown and that He will come suddenly like a thief who attacks in the night. The comparison of Christ's Second Coming to a thief is mentioned eight times in the New Testament, two of them in this chapter, to urge us to spiritual watchfulness and constant vigilance.

5.2.0.en: When the wicked people of the world are sunk in their material lusts and imagine that they are materially secure in these pleasures, their hearts suddenly fall in fear and terror at their destruction by the Second Coming of Christ, as the hour of labor comes upon a woman with child, and there will be no escape for them.

5.3.0.en: But the believers live in the light, that is, in goodness, and expect the coming of the Lord, and this knowledge of theirs must lead them to watchfulness and vigilance; and so that day will not surprise them as it surprises the others.

5.4.0.en: Light: an expression for the pure, good life lived by the children of God, and it is the opposite of darkness, which is a symbol of evil.

5.4.1.en: Day: an expression for the clear spiritual life, and it is the opposite of the night, which is a symbol of sin working in secret.

5.4.2.en: St. Paul affirms that all believers live a pure life and keep away from evil in preparation for the coming of Christ.

5.5.0.en: What is meant by sleep here is not the sleep of the body, but slackness or neglect in spiritual matters, remembering always that the Second Coming of Christ must take place.

5.6.0.en: There is no place for neglect and debauchery for those who belong to the light and to the day. The picture of night here suggests the heedlessness of one who sleeps by his own will, and likewise immersion in pleasures, especially the drinking of wine, and drunkenness also means being occupied with material things instead of God.

5.7.0.en: The sons of the day ought to be sober. Preparation by spiritual watchfulness requires arming ourselves with spiritual weapons to repel all the attacks of the adversary, the enemy of good. Here the Apostle Paul makes use of the picture of the Roman soldier at war: faith is the breastplate that protects the chest from the arrows of the enemy, which are doubt and hatred. Likewise love protects a person from anger and from being affected by the insults of others. And the helmet protects the head, the center of thoughts, so that all thought is on heavenly things and on the awaited salvation that we hope for.

5.8.0.en: The believers have been appointed to salvation, for we do not await wrath but the obtaining of salvation, which the Lord accomplished on the Cross in order to give it to us at His Second Coming.

5.9.0.en: Wake: alive, striving with spiritual watchfulness.

5.9.1.en: Sleep: we have ended our life and fallen asleep.

5.9.2.en: We have obtained the merits of salvation through our Redeemer Jesus Christ, so whether we are found alive or asleep at His Second Coming, we shall all live together with Him.

5.10.0.en: The Apostle closes this section as he closed verses (13-18) in the previous chapter, in which he also spoke of the resurrection and the Second Coming, with the same phrase, "comfort one another," for when we think of the Second Coming of Christ and the general resurrection we are comforted and comfort one another concerning those who have fallen asleep. And when we think of the day of the Lord we remind one another that God has not appointed us to wrath but to obtain salvation, so we are always joyful and comforted and strengthen one another by encouraging one another to worship and good works. This they were doing, but St. Paul wanted them to increase in it.

5.10.1.en: May we remember eternity with its comforts, joys and happiness, so that we are comforted and strengthened and advance in our spiritual life, and busy ourselves with prayers, praises, reading, meditations and works of mercy toward every person, so that we are ready to receive our heavenly Bridegroom, our Lord Jesus Christ.

5.11.1.en: Labour: serve in the various ministries in the Church.

5.11.2.en: Are over you: shepherd you and arrange all your needs.

5.11.3.en: Admonish you: teach you by preaching so that you keep away from evil and live with Christ. This epistle is one of the oldest writings of the New Testament, and in it St. Paul shows the importance of esteeming the shepherds of the Church, who include the bishops, the priests, the deacons and all the servants.

5.12.0.en: Esteem them very highly: esteeming the shepherds in love means:

5.12.1.en: 1- Obeying them and submitting to them.

5.12.3.en: 3- Helping them to complete their ministry.

5.12.4.en: Be at peace among yourselves: because Satan stirs up troubles and factions and, at times, the insubordination of some, as happened in the Church of Corinth, so the Apostle here directs them to the importance of holding fast to peace in the relationships of the believers with one another within the Church.

5.13.0.en: Warn: teach firmly and direct those who err to repentance.

5.13.1.en: Unruly: those who are not subject to the Church and who walk by their own ideas.

5.13.2.en: Comfort the feebleminded: those who are greatly distressed if they fall into a great sin or their sins are repeated, so they need to be encouraged to repent and begin anew, holding fast to Christ the Savior. Support the weak: those who fall into despair before afflictions or stumble at any improper act or problem, so they need support to continue their life with God.

5.13.3.en: Be patient toward all men: all people are liable to error or negligence, so they need longsuffering and gentleness from us.

5.13.4.en: The Apostle asks them to rebuke those who depart from the faith and the order of the Church, and at the same time to encourage those who doubt themselves and the weak who despair because of their many sins and the afflictions around them, and to continue showing their love with longsuffering toward all.

5.14.0.en: Practical Christianity is to bear the evil of others, and even to do good in return for evil; for love is what makes us bear with the wicked, and by good we quench every flame of sin.

5.15.0.en: He who makes the Lord the source of his joy can rejoice at all times, even in circumstances of sorrow. But the Christian who remains in a state of gloom and depression does not trust in the power of his God and His care and love.

5.16.0.en: We ought to walk through life with our hearts always lifted up to God, for prayer is fellowship with God, and when we pray at all times we share God in all the steps of our life's journey.

5.17.0.en: Thanksgiving in everything flows from our knowing that all the circumstances we pass through, with their sufferings and afflictions, come to us from God. God is the One who holds the reins of affairs, and He may at times permit unpleasant things for our good: "all things work together for good to them that love God" (Rom 8:28). So if we want to fulfill the will of God on our part and gladden His heart, we must live a life of surrender and thank Him in every condition, for every condition and in every condition.

5.17.1.en: The true Christian feels for the weak and hastens to their aid and to strengthen them without irritation or contempt, because love is what moves him toward all, so he does not think of himself but of others first, and feels his spiritual fatherhood and cares for the salvation of all.

5.18.0.en: The Holy Spirit appeared on the day of Pentecost in the form of tongues of fire, that is, a blazing flame, as a symbol of His activity and effectiveness, for He is a light that illumines the mind and a power that kindles the spirit of man. So anything that hinders the work of the Spirit in us we must guard against, and this means persisting in not repenting of sin, or slackness, negligence and preoccupation away from God.

5.19.0.en: Prophesyings: in the New Testament, prophecy means speaking about the coming Kingdom of God, that is, all the spiritual teachings and preparation for the Kingdom.

5.19.1.en: Here is a warning against despising preaching, as when we say, for example, that the preaching brought nothing new, or when we harden our hearts before the word of God.

5.20.0.en: Prove every counsel or teaching you hear: is it in agreement with the teachings of the Church, the Holy Bible and the guidance of the father of confession? If you find it good, hold fast to all that is good and reject everything else.

5.21.0.en: Let us abstain from every appearance of evil, or even any intention of it, however slight it may seem; for we may do something from which we mean no harm to anyone, yet it may cause another person for whom Christ died to stumble, so we must abstain from evil by doing it or even by merely intending to do it, that is, the intention of evil is counted as sin.

5.22.0.en: Sanctify you wholly: God is able to make you dedicated to Him and to fill your hearts with peace and to be your only aim.

5.22.1.en: May your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved: God establishes your whole being, spirit, soul and body, that you may live all your life for Him and be blameless on the day of judgment before Christ. The Apostle wishes for the work of God's grace in them to consecrate their lives to Him until their end.

5.23.0.en: God who called us is faithful and will continue His work in us and fulfill His promises, and He is the One who will keep us and perfect us until the day of the coming of the Lord: "he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ" (Phil 1:6).

5.24.0.en: The great Apostle of the Gentiles, in spite of the station he had reached among the Churches, felt in humility his need of the prayers of the believers. He prayed for them and desires that they in turn pray for him, and in this way fellowship is realized among all the believers.

5.25.0.en: Our greeting to one another must be holy, that is, sincere and free from hypocrisy. The Apostle here stresses sincerity when we greet one another.

5.26.0.en: The Apostle wanted to be sure that his letter would reach every person so that all might benefit from what it contains.

5.27.0.en: This is the form of the apostolic blessing which St. Paul uses, and this blessing contains all spiritual good and is sufficient for every need.

5.27.1.en: Take care to pray for everyone around you and for every problem you hear about, for prayer is mighty because it opens the mercies of God, who is able to do all things, and therefore also care for the prayers of others for you, for they support you in all your steps.
